column1: # Game profile of Diablo III: Eternal Collection (Switch, update 2.7.7.92380 = v1441792). Plays on the Mac (logos, the intro movie, hero creation, the Act I opening cinematic, the road into
# New Tristram, walking and fighting at 60 fps with sound)
# Blizzard's own engine (no Unreal: the survey's Unreal 4 marker is a false one), FMOD, SDK 8.2.0. The game's data are SNO assets in Blizzard's console packages (CPKs/*.cpk and
# Update/CPKs/*.cpk, not CRI's CPK: dm/gfx/tools/d3cpk.py); its shaders are control sections each followed by its code area in the zlib streams of those packages (shader_split.py d3cpk_shaders).
# The provisional profile's guesses held: no key needed changing

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory). The game sets no heap: it takes its memory as address regions in the alias region (nn::os::AllocateAddressRegion,
# 0.75 GB from main+0xa70 and 0.36 GB from main+0xa36c58 at boot) and maps them; on the Mac they reach alias +3.00 GB in seven minutes of play from a fresh save, within the 4.38 GB below.
# A 5 GB block with a large alias region (the NSP script's guess)
# the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 at boot (the NSP script's heap check): the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
